newsitem.title: UK: ACI Q1 1997 shows Air Traffic cargo up 8 pct.
newsitem.headline: ACI Q1 1997 shows Air Traffic cargo up 8 pct.

text.p: The tonnage of cargo passing through the world's airports climbed by eight percentin the first quarter of 1997 whilst passenger traffic rose five percent, the latest airport traffic report from the Geneva-based Airports Council International (ACI) showed.

....ACI Director of Economics Paul Benhkne observed "broad-based steady growth in passenger traffic occurred across all regions for the first quarter of 1997, showing a strong increase over a similar buoyant first quarter in 1996.
....Part of the increase could be attributed to the early Easter travel season falling within the first quarter" he added.
....Airports in Asia/Pacfic showed the highest cargo volume growth,up 14 percent, followed by the Middle East up nine percent, North America up eight percent and Europe up four percent.
....The report which contains data from 495 airports worldwide shows aircraft movements rose by two percent for the first three months of 1997.
....Cargo handled in airports in Africa and Latin America/Caribbean remained virtually unchanged up 0.7 and 0.5 percent respectively.
....First quarter passenger traffic growth was highest in Africa up nine percent, followed by Asia/Pacific and Europe, each up six percent.

....African and European airports saw a five percent rise in aircraft movements followed by Latin America/Caribbean up four percent, Asia/Pacific up three percent and North America up by eight percent.
- First Quarter 1997 with percentage changes from First Quarter 1996
